feedbackPairs.question: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
feedbackPairs.good: A process is an independent program in execution with its own memory space, file handles and resources. A thread is a unit of execution inside a process; threads of the same process share the heap and resources but each has its own stack and registers. Creating and switching threads is cheaper than processes, but shared memory means threads need synchronization like mutexes to avoid race conditions.
feedbackPairs.bad: Process is bigger and thread is smaller. Both run programs.

feedbackPairs.question: Explain how a database index speeds up queries and what it costs.
feedbackPairs.good: Most databases use a B-tree index: a sorted, balanced tree on the indexed column, so a lookup is O(log n) instead of a full table scan. It also helps range queries and ORDER BY. The cost is extra storage and slower writes, because every INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE must also update the index, so you index columns that are frequently filtered or joined on, not everything.
feedbackPairs.bad: Index makes the database fast. You should add index on all columns.

feedbackPairs.question: What is the event loop in Node.js?
feedbackPairs.good: Node runs JavaScript on a single thread. Async operations like I/O are handed to the OS or libuv's thread pool, and their callbacks are queued. The event loop repeatedly takes callbacks from these queues and runs them when the call stack is empty, in phases such as timers, poll and check. Promise callbacks go to the microtask queue, which is drained after each callback, before moving on.
feedbackPairs.bad: Event loop is a loop that runs events again and again.

feedbackPairs.question: How does JWT authentication work?
feedbackPairs.good: After login the server creates a token with a header, a payload with claims like user id and expiry, and a signature made with a secret. The client sends it on each request, usually in an httpOnly cookie or Authorization header. The server verifies the signature and expiry without a session lookup, which makes it stateless. Downsides: revocation is hard, so you use short expiry plus refresh tokens.
feedbackPairs.bad: JWT is a token. The user gets it and it is secure because it is encrypted.

feedbackPairs.question: Two users try to book the last seat at the same time. How do you prevent double booking?
feedbackPairs.good: Make the database the source of truth. Either lock the seat row in a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE so the second request waits and then sees it is taken, or use optimistic concurrency with a unique constraint on (show_id, seat_id) so the second insert fails and returns 409. I would add a short hold with an expiry so abandoned checkouts free the seat, and make the booking endpoint idempotent so client retries do not create duplicates.
feedbackPairs.bad: I will check if the seat is free in the code and then book it. If it is booked I show an error.

feedbackPairs.question: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
feedbackPairs.good: TCP is connection-oriented: it does a three-way handshake and guarantees ordered, reliable delivery with retransmission, flow control and congestion control. UDP is connectionless and just sends datagrams with no delivery or ordering guarantee, so it has lower overhead and latency. TCP fits web pages and file transfer; UDP fits video calls, games and DNS where speed matters more than every packet.
feedbackPairs.bad: TCP is used in internet and UDP is also used in internet but different.

feedbackPairs.question: Tell me about a time you worked under a tight deadline.
feedbackPairs.good: In my internship we had four days to ship a reconciliation report before a client audit. I split the work into must-have and nice-to-have, agreed the scope with my lead on day one, and wrote the core query first so we had something working early. I flagged on day three that the export would not be ready and we shipped CSV instead. We met the audit, and I learned to raise risks early instead of hoping to catch up.
feedbackPairs.bad: I always work hard so deadlines are not a problem for me.

feedbackPairs.question: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
feedbackPairs.good: RAG grounds an LLM's answer in external data. Documents are split into chunks and embedded into vectors. At query time the question is embedded, the most similar chunks are retrieved by vector similarity and added to the prompt, and the model answers using them. It reduces hallucination and lets the model use private or fresh data without retraining. Quality depends on chunking, the embedding model and retrieval evaluation.
feedbackPairs.bad: RAG is a type of AI model that is better than ChatGPT.
